angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 313,065 km at 133.50 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.4906 +/- 0.0148 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 133.50 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.45 +/- 0.08 solar radii from Rappaport et al. 2013, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of KOI-1843.03 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract): 313,065 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.46 +/- 0.08 solar masses from Rappaport et al. 2013, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of KOI-1843.03 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3584 +/- 65 K from Rappaport et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KOI-1843.03 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rappaport et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KOI-1843.03 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-974.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.794, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
